text:
incident-bot: 🔔 Pager: genqueue-errors-high (us-west-prod) — error_rate > 5% for 3m. Paging @maya (oncall) and @sam (sre). See /alerts/GENQ-923.
maya (oncall): on it. jumping into the runbook. starting a zoom: https://zoom.redwood/abc123
sam (sre): joining. quick check — are we seeing 5xx on /v1/generate or streaming only?
maya (oncall): both. spikes in 503 and 504 across generation and streaming gateways. tail shows KV cache misses and model instance OOM retries.
jo (platform): observing a correlated surge of long-lived connections to prod-gpu-pool-7, GC/oom churn. metrics: cpu 85%, gpu mem 98% on 7/8 nodes.
carla (comms): we should draft a short initial statuspage and customer DM. I can put a first-pass notice below, pls edit. we need to confirm scope before publish.
sam (sre): provisional mitigation: 1) toggle fallback routing to model-variant 'gen-small-2024' for non-priority routes, 2) cordon two problematic nodes, 3) evict long prefix caches. Starting routing change now.
maya (oncall): sam — go for routing. tagging playback if latency regression. I'll monitor error rate.
ops-runbook-bot: ACTION: started runbook "genqueue-high-errors" (runbook id: RB-77). Assigned to maya, sam. ETA steps logged.
carla (comms): DRAFT statuspage (initial):
---
We are investigating elevated error rates for generation and streaming in the us-west region. Some requests may receive 503/504 errors or experience higher latency. Engineers are actively mitigating; a partial routing fallback has been enacted to reduce failed requests. We will post updates every 15 minutes or when there is a material change.
Impacted services: text generation (POST /v1/generate), streaming endpoints (POST /v1/stream).
Customer impact: intermittent failed requests and increased latency in us-west. No authenticated data exposure identified.
---
Please review and flag anything to remove.
dan (legal): quick note — ok to publish as-is. keep the phrasing "no authenticated data exposure identified" — don't speculate beyond that. fine to mention fallback routing.
jo (platform): routing switched: traffic for low-priority keys -> gen-small-2024; high-tier (dedicated customers + reserved capacity) remain pinned to prod variants. Early signal: error rate down ~40% on low-priority cohort.
maya (oncall): monitoring: overall error rate fell to 3.1% after routing change. still seeing timeouts from 2 nodes (gpu-7a, gpu-7b). I've started cordon/drain on gpu-7b.
sam (sre): cordon/drain in progress on gpu-7b. suspected memory leak in nightly build; rolling back last patch to model-serving infra on those nodes.
carla (comms): updated statuspage (15m):
---
Update (15:22 UTC): We have implemented a routing fallback for lower-priority traffic which has reduced the error rate. We are continuing to drain and remediate a subset of GPU nodes experiencing memory pressure. High-priority customers on Dedicated remain unaffected by the fallback. We will provide another update within 15 minutes or sooner.
---
Would you like me to publish now?
maya (oncall): publish. include link to status page entry and note that we will follow with customer DMs for affected orgs. go ahead.
carla (comms): publishing initial and update. Posted to status.redwood.com/incidents/GENQ-923
ops-runbook-bot: NOTE: mitigation step "rollback-serving-patch" executed by sam at 15:30 UTC.
sam (sre): rollback succeeded on gpu-7a/7b. rechecked memory metrics — stabilization visible. moving to observe for 10m.
jo (platform): KV cache hotset purge completed; prefix cache warming in progress. This should reduce sudden backend pressure for repeated long prefixes.
maya (oncall): error rate down to 0.4% and latency returning to baseline. starting post-incident checklist and root-cause capture.
carla (comms): DRAFT resolved notice:
---
Resolved (15:45 UTC): The elevated error rate affecting generation and streaming in us-west has been resolved. Root cause: memory regression in a recent serving patch causing OOM retries on a subset of GPU nodes. Mitigations applied: routing fallback for lower-priority traffic, rollback of the problematic serving patch, and node drains. Customer impact: intermittent 503/504 errors and increased latency for some requests during the incident window. No evidence of data exposure. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support.
---
ok to publish this resolved message?
dan (legal): approved.
carla (comms): published resolved notice and sent targeted DMs to affected customers list (internal id: custlist-genq-1789). Logged postmortem ping to #postmortems.
maya (oncall): closing pager. running post-incident telemetry capture and adding notes to incident ticket: INC-2024-1789. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
sam (sre): adding follow-ups: (1) revert risky nightly infra build from canary, (2) add memory regression tests, (3) tune eviction policy for KV prefix cache. will assign owners.
carla (comms): follow-up: coordinate postmortem timeline and customer-facing summary. aiming for a short customer note in 48 hours, full postmortem in 7 days.
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK COMPLETE: status changed to RESOLVED. Incident duration: 00:45.
maya (oncall): signing off from zoom. leaving notes in ticket. good job team.
